name: Elkanah (Son of Korah, a Korahite Levite)
title: Korahite Levite
summary: Elkanah was a son of Korah and belonged to the Korahite branch of the tribe of Levi. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Exodus and 1 Chronicles as part of Korah's descendants, who survived Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron. The Korahites later became known as important temple servants and singers in Israelite worship.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Korah's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Elkanah is listed as one of the sons of Korah in the genealogy of the tribe of Levi, along with his brothers Assir and Abiasaph.

keyEvents.title: Korah's Rebellion
keyEvents.description: Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron led to the earth opening up and swallowing the rebels, but Korah's sons, including Elkanah, did not perish.

keyEvents.title: The Levitical service of the Korahites
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Korah, to whom Elkanah belonged, were assigned important roles in Levitical service and are mentioned in the genealogical records of Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: The Korahites as gatekeepers
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Korah, including the line of Elkanah, served as gatekeepers and guards at the tabernacle and later at the temple.

keyEvents.title: The singing service of the Korahites
keyEvents.description: The Korahites became known for their role in temple music. Several psalms are attributed to the sons of Korah, reflecting the spiritual heritage of this lineage.
